newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian democracy campaigner arrested - papers.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian democracy campaigner arrested - papers.

text.p: Nigerian activist Frederick Fasehun has been detained by security forces in a raid on his Lagos home, local newspapers said on Thursday.
The independent Guardian said Fasehun, a medical doctor, was taken away on Wednesday morning after a police search of his house and private hospital.
Fasehun took over as chairman of the umbrella Campaign for Democracy from Beko Ransome-Kuti who in 1995 was given a 15-year prison sentence for his part in alleged coup plot.
Nigeria's commercial capital, Lagos, is in a state of high tension following two bomb explosions in less than a week which have seriously injured over a dozen soldiers.
Nobody has claimed responsibility for the attacks but police in November accused opponents of the military government of being behind a bungled car-bomb which killed the three would-be bombers.
Dozens of opposition figures are detained in Africa's most populous nation, which has become a pariah state for alleged human rights abuses and lack of democracy.
